points.verdict: KILL: halving active width is ~2x SLOWER; dispatch/launch and small-GEMM overhead dominate
KILL: slower than dense Arm-A; 32 unrolled expert streams x 8 levels defeats the GPU
KILLED BY EVIDENCE (never run): monotone degradation M8->M16->M32 plus >20 min projected compile

conclusion: Active-width subdivision at fixed stored K is saturated at M8 top1. The fitted width curve (T = 29.8 + 0.0575*Kactive) only holds when reducing active experts at fixed M (larger streams). Increasing M shrinks per-expert GEMMs and multiplies kernel/launch count; the overhead term grows faster than the arithmetic term shrinks.
